posts.cooked:
PL626 Compound Xi states "Whenever a hero uses a power, Spite deals them 2 toxic damage etc. etc." - so putting the name of that hero into the sentence and replacing "them" with the name again normally makes perfect sense, e.g. "Whenever Legacy uses a power, Spite deals Legacy 2 toxic damage".  But when it becomes "Whenever the Sentinels use a power, Spite deals the Sentinels 2 damage", it becomes a bit of a problem.  The card does NOT explicitly deal the damage to the character card which used the power, so this means you could have Mainstay keep taking the damage even while you use The Idealist's power every turn.  Is this as it's intended to be?  It seems wrong somehow.

Also, to be more esoteric, say that Spite starts with the Lost Child in play, and then Mainstay uses Block on his turn.  When the Sentinels's next turn starts, is Block still in effect when Mainstay chooses to take damage saving the Child?  Does the answer change if the Lost Child enters play after Block is used?

One last question, which I'm sure has been asked and answered before, but I have no idea how you'd search for it...when Spite flips and destroys all Victims not in the Safehouse, does he regain HP for their deaths, then take the damage for those that were safe?  Or does it happen in some other order?

posts.cooked: My understanding is that the Sentinels have the powers collectively.  So the damage goes to the hero - The Sentinels collectively - and gets pushed onto whichever target you choose.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Yep, same as Infection - one hero is Infected, but as the Sentinels are collectively one hero, you then choose which of the four individuals recieves the actual Infection. Same goes for anything else which targets the Sentinels as a "hero".

On Spite flipping - the condition for him hitting himself for Victim damage is that he has flipped - once he's flipped, he no longer lifetaps, and the Safehouse specifically triggers on his "flipped to Drug-Wracked Monstrosity side". So he'll then hit himself for "Victims x 5" damage and soak H-2 points of the damage (from that drug that lets him soak once per turn) but also deal +1 damage to himself (from the damage-buffing drug). If H=3 then the two cancel each other out.

Do them in the order that you think best, it's a rule15/Order of Operations thing, it's not happening because it's the start of the turn, that was just the instruction to flip him.

 

But saying that flipping a card changes when they entered play is jibber jabber. Do Omintron's ongoing trigger before he flips because they were in play before the flipped side? What about the Matriarch's birds? Or Voss' minions?

The character/rules card only enters play once, at the start of the game.

posts.cooked:
Matchstickman:

But saying that flipping a card changes when they entered play is jibber jabber. Do Omintron's ongoing trigger before he flips because they were in play before the flipped side?

That's not precisely what I meant.  I know that it doesn't change the order of the cards entering play; my thought was that a previously-in-play "when the villain character card flips" effect might conceivably happen the very instant that the flip occurs, before any text from the newly-flipped side can be applied.  Imagine that the Safe house goes "ding" as soon as the card is perpendicular to the table, whereas the text doesn't appear until it lies flat on the new side.  May not be how it works, but I thought it seemed logical.  It would not apply to any other triggers except maybe Blade and Skinweaver gaining HP when they flip for hitting 0; I don't think there's another card which isn't the villain character card but has effects that happen when that card flips.
